text.p: Hoiupank said on Thursday its June net profit was a record 18.8 million kroons compared to 18.1 million kroons in May.
The bank's current year profit was 94.9 million kroons at the end of June, it added in a statement.
The current year profit makes up 83.8 percent of its 1997 profit forecast.
The bank has said earlier it would revise its earlier forecast only after the half-year results were audited.
Assets grew by 133.8 million kroons or 2.2 percent to 6.35 billion kroons in June.
The assets have grown by over two billion kroons or 46.5 percent in the first half year.
Total deposits grew 114.7 million kroons or 2.7 percent in June to 4.4 billion kroons. Demand deposits grew by nine percent or 263.2 million kroons in June to 3.2 billion kroons.
Deposits have grown by 1.3 billion kroons or 41.4 percent in six months.
During the six months, the loan portfolio has grown 51 percent or 1.2 billion kroons to 3.37 billion kroons.
The interest revenues in six months were 259.7 million kroons and interest expenditures 89.2 million kroons. The net interest revenues were 170.5 million kroons.
Administrative costs were 125.9 million kroons in six months compared to 78.7 million kroons in the same period last year.
"1997 half year net profit is gained by quicker rise in revenues in front of expenditures," the bank added.
